source_refs.note: Book p. 36-38: heading 2.3 The Chain Rule; the book prints no text of its own under it (subtopics 2.3.1-2.3.3 follow)

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Ab tak hum aise functions ka derivative nikal sakte hain jaise sin x ya x^2 - x, aur in ke jor, zarb aur taqseem ka bhi. Lekin zara socho: agar ek function doosre function ke andar baitha ho, jaise sin(x^2 - x), to kya karein? Yahan sin ke andar poora x^2 - x baitha hai. Aise functions ke liye ek naya aur bohat taaqatwar rule chahiye: Chain Rule. Yeh calculus ka shayad sab se zyada istemal hone wala rule hai; aage har unit mein aap ise baar baar lagayenge.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab is heading ke neeche apni koi ibarat nahin likhti; seedha 2.3.1 shuru ho jata hai. Yeh chhota sa taaruf hamari taraf se hai, taa ke aap ko pata ho ke aage kya aa raha hai.
Chain rule ka khulasa ek jumle mein: pehle bahar wale function ka derivative lo, andar wale function ko us ke andar waisa hi rehne do, phir andar wale function ke derivative se zarb do.
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy}{du} \cdot \dfrac{du}{dx}\]
Zanjeer (chain) ki tarah: ek kari doosri kari se juri hai. Agar y, u ke saath badalta hai aur u, x ke saath, to y, x ke saath kitna badlega? Dono tabdeeliyon ko zarb kar do.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is section mein teen hisse hain:
1. 2.3.1 Composition of Functions: function ke andar function (composition) kya hota hai, aur Theorem 1, yani Chain Rule. Is ka istemal Example 3 mein hoga.
2. 2.3.2 Parametric Equations: jab \(x\) aur \(y\) dono kisi teesre variable \(t\) mein diye hon (jaise kisi cheez ki position waqt \(t\) ke saath), to chain rule se \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\) milta hai (Example 4).
3. 2.3.3 Implicit Differentiation: jab \(y\) ko \(x\) ke formula ki shakal mein likhna mushkil ho, to poori relation ko term by term differentiate karte hain, aur har us term par chain rule lagate hain jis mein \(y\) ho (Example 5).

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Shuru karne se pehle 2.1 aur 2.2 ki cheezein taaza kar lijiye: power rule, product rule, quotient rule aur chhe trigonometric derivatives. Chain rule in ki jagah nahin leta, balke in ke saath mil kar kaam karta hai. Har chain rule ke sawal mein andar aur bahar ke derivatives inhi purane rules se aate hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: In mein se kaun se functions 'function ke andar function' hain: \(x^{2}\sin x\), \(\sin(x^{2})\), \((x + 1)^{7}\), \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\)? (Jawab: \(\sin(x^{2})\) aur \((x + 1)^{7}\). Baqi do mein functions zarb ya taqseem ho rahe hain, ek doosre ke andar nahin.)
